how_to_mine: Run this where POST requests work, such as a Python script with requests. 1) POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_transaction/ with JSON: {"filters":{"keywords":["NovaSeq"],"recipient_search_text":["Illumina"],"award_type_codes":["A","B","C","D"],"time_period":[{"start_date":"2023-01-01","end_date":"2026-10-01"}]},"fields":["Award ID","Mod","Recipient Name","Transaction Amount","Action Date","Transaction Description","Awarding Agency","Award Type"],"sort":"Action Date","order":"asc","limit":100,"page":1}. Page through the results to the 1,000-transaction cap. Repeat with keywords S4, 25B, 10B, 1.5B, 35B and 6000. Also repeat with award_type_codes for IDV (IDV_A to IDV_E) and for purchase orders. 2) Classify each line by regex. 6000 means S1, S2, S4, SP or 6000 in the text. X means 1.5B, 10B, 25B, 35B or NovaSeq X. 3) Report dollars and counts by half-year. Where a description gives a kit quantity or a catalog number (20012866 is S4-300, per the Texas A&M PO), compute the unit price and compare it with list. 4) Flag any 35B line as an early signal of price or launch timing. Note that many federal descriptions are generic (for example 'reagents'), so the share of classifiable lines may be low. Use PIID/Award ID to pull the parent award from the Award endpoint if needed. Add the DoD, VA and NIH/HHS awarding agencies if a filter is needed.
